analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. Units 4 and 5 show the base text at lines 829-1195. Unit 6 shows the head text from line 1 with a 'Last updated: 2026-10-20' header. The visible head excerpt (lines 1-403) covers context, calibration, deadlines and the request flow, and is mostly narrative. No source, config, key handling, or wire contract is altered in the supplied units.

I saw no head-side equivalent of the base MiMo, Flash-Next and Bonsai sections. The supplied head excerpt stops at line 403, so those sections were either moved or removed, or the excerpt was truncated. I cannot confirm which. This is a coverage limit and not evidence that anything is unsafe.

Relevant threat IDs touched by the prose: T-041 and TB-007 (prefix cache, encrypted SSD store), T-010 and T-029 (cancellation/idle, retirement-before-release claims), T-050 (media decode, 'neither path writes the payload to disk'), A-001, and T-007/T-027 (model correctness). The documents state that the new MiMo, SSD and calibration behaviors are unqualified or candidate-only and make no production claims. The claim that media stays target-only and noncacheable is consistent with T-041 and does not widen at-rest exposure.

The next pass should check the remainder of the head file (lines 404 onward) and whether the MiMo/Bonsai sections persist. It should also check whether other changed files, such as the code and the threat-model YAML, back the doc statements about retained owners, the SSD default for MiMo, and calibration. No security regression is evident from docs alone. needs_deeper_review is set true only because the head text is truncated.
